NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI semiconductor value chain, critically dependent on TSMC for advanced node fabrication and HBM suppliers like SK Hynix for memory integration, with virtually no alternative foundry options for its leading-edge products. On the downstream side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a small number of hyperscalers and cloud providers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, Amazon) who are racing to build AI infrastructure, creating both enormous demand tailwinds and significant customer concentration risk.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the pinnacle of a complex, globally distributed supply chain, acting primarily as a designer and assembler that relies on a concentrated set of Asian foundries and component suppliers — most critically TSMC for advanced silicon — while distributing its vertically integrated hardware and services ecosystem through carriers, retailers, and platform partners worldwide. Its downstream is uniquely diversified across consumer end-markets (iPhone, Mac, iPad, Wearables) and a high-margin Services segment that monetizes its 2+ billion active device installed base through the App Store, licensing, and content.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of a capital-intensive semiconductor supply chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of equipment suppliers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its advanced DRAM and 3D NAND manufacturing nodes. On the demand side, Micron is increasingly exposed to AI-driven datacenter spending through HBM and data center DRAM shipments to hyperscalers and NVIDIA, while maintaining broad diversification across mobile, client PC, and automotive end markets.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: Arm Holdings occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP supply chain, monetizing its CPU, GPU, and systems IP through royalty and licensing fees paid by virtually every major chip designer globally rather than manufacturing silicon itself. Its upstream dependencies are primarily on EDA software vendors like Cadence and Synopsys, while its downstream relationships span hyperscalers, fabless chip companies, and OEMs — making Arm a foundational and largely irreplaceable layer of the global semiconductor ecosystem.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at a critical juncture in the data infrastructure supply chain, designing high-performance ASICs, Ethernet, and storage semiconductors that are fabless and manufactured primarily at TSMC on advanced nodes. Its downstream exposure is increasingly concentrated in hyperscaler cloud customers (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) who are driving significant custom ASIC demand for AI workloads, while also serving networking OEMs and storage hardware manufacturers.
